answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence reaching a coalition must cross its boundary. A sybil cluster with few external attestations is an island of low conductance: walks rarely enter it, limiting the trust mass it can accumulate. With normalized, capped vote weights, cut-based transitivity bounds its aggregate voting power by boundary flow, even if internal links form a dense vine; bounded walks cannot wander indefinitely to amplify it.
